scope: CLI grammar, argument ambiguity, repeats/missing values/unknown flags, defaults and backward-compatible status flags (src/cli/arguments.ts, src/cli.ts argument dispatch and usage text, CLI flag path into src/settings/load.ts). Read-only review; experiments in /tmp/rev39 only.

findings.title: Empty flag value accepted and silently ignored: status --url "" falls back to the default/env endpoint
findings.evidence: value() at src/cli/arguments.ts:48-53 only rejects an exhausted iterator, so "" is returned as a legal value; status() passes it through at src/cli/arguments.ts:66 as overrides.SWARMFORGE_URL="". setValue treats an empty value as unset (src/settings/load.ts:662 `if (value === "") return;`) and resolveClientSettings then falls back to SWARMFORGE_URL or DEFAULT_CLIENT_URL = http://127.0.0.1:8787/mcp (src/settings/load.ts:871). Regression vs baseline 5672ead, where argumentsFor() did `if (!value) throw new Error("--url requires an endpoint")`.
findings.reproduction: Bun 1.4.2, detached checkout at target. `status --url "" --json` -> stderr "SwarmForge: Unable to connect. Is the computer able to access the url?", exit 1 (default endpoint attempted, no usage error). With SWARMFORGE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:9/mcp the empty override is discarded entirely, same message/exit. `status --config ""` -> "Cannot read <cwd>: EISDIR", exit 1; `status --env-file ""` -> "Cannot read environment file <cwd>: EISDIR", exit 1.
findings.recommendation: In value() refuse an empty next token: `if (next.value === "") throw new UsageError(`${flag} requires ${noun}`)`, restoring the baseline refusal and preventing a silently different endpoint target.

findings.title: A flag in a value position is consumed as the value, silently voiding serve --check-config
findings.evidence: value() takes the next token unconditionally (src/cli/arguments.ts:48-53; call sites :66,:68,:70,:93,:94,:95,:118,:119), while the config action position deliberately rejects a leading flag at src/cli/arguments.ts:110. So `serve --config --check-config` parses to {checkConfig:false, configPath:"--check-config"} and reaches serveCommand (src/cli.ts:194-206) as a normal serve, contradicting the documented no-state guarantee in the usage text (src/cli.ts:52-53).
findings.reproduction: `serve --config --check-config` -> "SwarmForge: Config file not found: <cwd>/--check-config", exit 1; `serve --env-file --check-config` -> "Environment file not found: <cwd>/--check-config", exit 1; `status --url --json` -> "Client endpoint must use http or https: --json", exit 1 (the --json request is lost). Correct orders (`--check-config --config FILE`, `--config FILE --check-config`) both parse checkConfig:true. Verified no database/lock/listener was created (state dir stayed empty).
findings.recommendation: Treat a next token beginning with '-' as a missing value inside value(), mirroring src/cli/arguments.ts:110; the same guard also fixes the empty-value case.

findings.title: --version/--help discard all remaining arguments; -h/-V undocumented
findings.evidence: parseArguments returns {kind:"version"} at src/cli/arguments.ts:145 and {kind:"help"} at :144 (and :106-108 for `config --help`) before the rest of argv is scanned, so trailing unknown arguments are silently ignored (exit 0), unlike the strict unknown-argument refusal elsewhere. usage (src/cli.ts:37-38,54-55) lists only --version/--help although -V/-h are accepted (src/cli/arguments.ts:41,145).
findings.reproduction: Pure parser probe: parseArguments(["-V","--nonsense"]) = {kind:"version"}; parseArguments(["--version","status"]) = {kind:"version"}; both exit 0 through src/cli.ts:314-321.
findings.recommendation: Reject leftover arguments after help/version with a usage error, or document that they are ignored, and list -h/-V in usage.

notes: Repeats: --url/--config are last-wins silently (undocumented but conventional); --json/--no-interactive/--check-config idempotent; --env-file accumulates in order as documented.
No --flag=value form and no `--` terminator are accepted; `--url=http://a/mcp` and `-- --json` are refused. Consistency observation only.

mcpEndpoint no longer validates the scheme itself (src/cli.ts:138-142) but resolveClientSettings still rejects non-http/https (src/settings/load.ts:874-887), preserving baseline behaviour for ftp://host/mcp.
config path|show|validate correctly refuse a missing action, a flag in the action position, an unknown action and a second action.
